hero.headline: Jill Biden says Trump pardon was needed to protect Hunter from targeting
hero.teaser: Former first lady defends her stepson's pardon in new interview, citing concerns about incoming administration.
hero.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden has defended the presidential pardon issued to her stepson, Hunter Biden, explaining that the decision became necessary after Donald Trump's election victory.

In a recent interview, Jill Biden stated that the circumstances surrounding the pardon changed once Trump won the presidency. "When [President] Trump was elected, things changed, and we knew that he would target Hunter, and we just could not let our son go to jail on a charge that no one would," she said.

The pardon, issued by former President Joe Biden before leaving office, covered federal charges that had been brought against Hunter Biden. According to Jill Biden's account, the family's decision to support the pardon was motivated by concerns about how Trump might use his position to pursue her stepson.

Jill Biden's comments suggest that the pardon was partly a protective measure against potential future prosecution. She emphasized that Hunter faced charges that were not typically prosecuted against others, implying the case against him was unusual or politically motivated.

The former first lady's remarks come as she prepares to release a new memoir titled "View from the East Wing," which documents her experiences during her time in the White House. The book is expected to include her perspective on her husband's 2024 presidential campaign and his decision to withdraw from the race.

Jill Biden has remained a steadfast supporter of her husband throughout his long political career. However, her recent comments about the pardon have drawn scrutiny from some observers. A former spokesperson for Jill Biden suggested that her current statements about events in the White House may have damaged her credibility, noting that she is now saying things "completely different" from what she said previously.

The pardon decision sparked considerable public debate when it was announced. While some viewed it as a father protecting his son from legal jeopardy, others criticized it as an abuse of presidential power. The former first lady's explanation that Trump would have targeted Hunter appears to be her fullest public justification for supporting the controversial pardon.

Jill Biden's upcoming memoir is likely to provide additional context about the pardon decision and other significant moments from the Biden presidency. Her willingness to discuss the pardon in interviews suggests she intends to address the controversy directly in the book, offering her perspective on one of the most debated decisions of the Biden administration's final days.

cards.headline: Iran suspends negotiations with US, threatens to close Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
Iran has suspended negotiations with the United States and threatened to completely block the Strait of Hormuz, according to state media reports. The announcement marks a significant collapse in diplomatic efforts that had been conducted through intermediaries in recent weeks.

The breakdown in talks comes after a tumultuous period of mixed signals and escalating military confrontations. For weeks, the US and Iran had maintained a ceasefire that began in early April, though sporadic exchanges of fire continued throughout May. Negotiations aimed at a more durable agreement had stalled repeatedly as both sides demanded concessions.

The Trump administration had been pushing hard for a deal. Trump requested changes to a proposed agreement, citing issues related to the Strait of Hormuz and the removal of highly enriched uranium. On one occasion, Trump announced that "great progress" had been made toward a complete agreement and paused a military operation called Project Freedom to allow space for peace negotiations. However, hours later he threatened that if Iran did not agree to terms, "the bombing starts, and it will be, sadly, at a much higher level and intensity than it was before."

According to reporting, Washington and Tehran had been close to agreeing on a one-page memorandum of understanding to end the war, with the US expecting Iran to respond to key points within 48 hours. However, those efforts ultimately failed to produce results.

The military situation remained volatile throughout negotiations. The US military said it destroyed Iranian small boats and intercepted incoming cruise missiles and drones. Iran denied these claims but acknowledged firing at commercial vessels and seizing two container ships since the ceasefire began. The Pentagon stated that Iran's attacks had fallen below the threshold of restarting major combat operations.

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical waterway through which a substantial portion of global oil shipments pass. Iran's threat to close the strait represents a major escalation in tensions between the two nations. Oil prices have fluctuated dramatically during the conflict, rising to $114 per barrel at one point and falling to around $97 as negotiations appeared to progress.

Trump faced pressure from declining poll numbers and appeals from Gulf allies to resolve the conflict before it caused further damage to the global economy. However, commentators noted that the self-proclaimed master dealmaker appeared to be sabotaging his own negotiations. Iran, strengthened by its military performance during the war, had become better positioned to demand concessions than before the conflict began.

The suspension of talks leaves the path forward uncertain. Both countries continue military operations, and Iran's decision to walk away from negotiations suggests the conflict may intensify further before any diplomatic resolution can be reached.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Jump as Iran Says It Will Stop U.S. Talks and Block Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
Oil prices rose sharply following escalating military strikes between Israel and Iran in the Middle East, with crude climbing more than 3 percent as energy markets reacted to heightened geopolitical tensions and threats to critical shipping routes.

The escalation centered on attacks against energy infrastructure. Israel targeted Iran's South Pars gasfield, prompting Iranian retaliation against facilities in Qatar. QatarEnergy reported that Iranian strikes caused "extensive damage" to Ras Laffan, the world's largest liquefied natural gas facility, damaging equipment responsible for 17 percent of the company's LNG export capacity. The company estimated repairs would take three to five years.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, initially spiked 10 percent to $119 a barrel before settling at $110, representing a 3.3 percent gain. Crude prices have surged 60 percent since the conflict began on February 28. European gas prices jumped dramatically, with Dutch wholesale gas rising 24 percent to 68 euros per megawatt hour, its highest level since December 2022. UK gas prices more than doubled since late February, raising concerns about household bills.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies. Any prolonged disruption could significantly affect worldwide oil supplies and prices. Richard Meade, editor-in-chief of Lloyd's List Intelligence, warned that the first confirmed strike on an operational gasfield marked a significant escalation, expanding risks to the entire Middle East Gulf energy and logistics system beyond just the strait.

Stock markets reflected the uncertainty worldwide. Japan's Nikkei tumbled 3.4 percent, South Korea's Kospi fell 2.7 percent, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped 2 percent. European markets followed suit, with the UK's FTSE 100 declining 2.35 percent. Wall Street opened lower as investors weighed rising oil prices against recent technology stock gains.

Energy analysts warned of broader economic consequences. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said fears of a sustained energy shock have resurfaced, noting that the prospect of prolonged conflict threatens economies across the region and worldwide through higher energy prices.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at consulting firm RSM UK, cautioned that elevated energy prices could trigger inflationary pressures, potentially pushing inflation toward 5 percent if prices remained high through summer. Such increases could prompt interest rate hikes from the Bank of England, with money markets now fully pricing in a quarter-point rise by July.

Major European airlines, including Lufthansa, announced that ticket prices would rise if fuel cost increases persisted for months. The energy consultancy Wood Mackenzie said the attacks had fundamentally altered the global gas market outlook, as disruption at the Qatari facility could exceed initial two-month expectations, with each additional month removing about 1.5 percent from annual global LNG availability.

cards.headline: Israel Orders Strikes on Beirut Suburbs as Conflict With Hezbollah Intensifies
cards.body:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the Israeli military to attack the southern suburbs of Beirut, a stronghold of the Iran-backed militant group Hezbollah. The announcement prompted thousands of residents to flee the area after Israel issued evacuation warnings for Dahieh and other neighborhoods in the capital's outskirts.

The strikes represent a significant escalation in Israel's military campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Netanyahu said the attacks were in response to Hezbollah assaults on Israeli civilians. The expansion of military operations into Beirut's suburbs marks a new phase in the conflict, bringing the fighting directly to Lebanon's capital city for the first time in this campaign.

Israel issued sweeping displacement orders affecting nearly a million people. The military instructed residents up to 25 miles from the border to head north of the Zahrani River, covering major cities including Nabatieh and dozens of villages. An evacuation order was also issued for a neighborhood in central Beirut near restaurants, where the Israeli military said it would strike a building.

The escalation followed Hezbollah's most intense attacks yet on Israel. The group, in coordination with Iran for the first time, launched successive volleys of rockets and drone swarms in what it called "Operation Chewed Wheat." Hezbollah fired more than 200 rockets toward Israeli territory, including at military bases in Haifa, Tel Aviv and Beersheba. Most projectiles were intercepted or fell into open areas, injuring two people.

Israeli warplanes responded immediately with intense bombardment of Beirut's southern suburbs and southern Lebanon. The Lebanese health ministry said 70 people were killed in Israeli strikes on Thursday. Among the dead were two academics, Hussein Bazzi and Murtadha Sarour, killed in an attack on the Lebanese University campus. At least 17 people were injured in strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, with more casualties expected.

Israel struck two buildings in central Beirut, leveling them after warning residents to evacuate. One building in the Zouq Blat neighborhood sat next to a shelter hosting displaced people, causing large crowds to gather in central Beirut's main square seeking shelter. The other building was located near the prime minister's office, UN agencies and foreign embassies.

In Israeli border communities, residents described a harrowing night. "Last night was a bit crazy," said Daniel Dorfman, a 43-year-old from Metula near the Lebanese border. "I don't get anxious usually but all the walls were shaking."

The exchange marked the most severe escalation in the 10-day conflict between Israel and Hezbollah. Human rights groups condemned the displacement orders as forced displacement that could amount to war crimes. They said Israeli military should still attempt to prevent civilian harm, even if civilians did not evacuate.

The escalation complicates diplomatic efforts to contain the wider regional conflict involving Iran and the United States.

cards.headline: Hezbollah signals readiness for immediate ceasefire with Israel
cards.teaser: Lebanese parliament speaker tells Trump administration that Hezbollah will accept full ceasefire and guarantee its implementation.
cards.body:
Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri conveyed to the Trump administration that Hezbollah is prepared for a full and immediate ceasefire with Israel. Berri's adviser Ali Hamdan confirmed the communication took place on Sunday and stated that Hezbollah would guarantee implementation of any agreement.

The signal comes as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered strikes on Beirut's Dahieh suburb, a Hezbollah stronghold, in response to attacks on Israeli civilians. Iran's negotiators continue discussions aimed at resolving the broader regional conflict.

cards.headline: Trump administration closes AI chip export loophole for Chinese-owned firms
cards.teaser: Commerce Department clarifies that licenses are required to sell advanced chips to companies with Chinese parents, regardless of location.
cards.body:
The Trump administration issued new Commerce Department guidance on Sunday to tighten restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chip exports. The clarification requires licenses for sales of these chips to firms with Chinese parent companies, even if the purchasing entity operates outside China or other restricted countries.

The move addresses a gap officials identified in 2023 export control requirements. By extending restrictions based on corporate ownership rather than just the physical location of the buyer, the administration aims to prevent companies from circumventing existing limitations on advanced chip sales.

cards.headline: US and Iran Exchange Attacks as Regional Conflict Continues
cards.teaser: The United States and Iran traded attacks as an unconfirmed report suggested Iran may stop negotiations with Washington.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have exchanged military strikes around the Strait of Hormuz, with the US targeting Iranian radar sites and Iran attacking American forces in Kuwait. These strikes represent the latest in a series of sporadic exchanges since a ceasefire took effect in early April, as negotiations toward a more lasting agreement continue.

Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered military strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, a Hezbollah stronghold, in response to attacks on Israeli civilians. Israel has issued evacuation orders for the area. The convergence of these conflicts across the Middle East involves multiple parties and has caused significant regional instability.

cards.headline: Ethiopia Holds National Election Amid Security Concerns and Regional Tensions
cards.teaser: Voting suspended in parts of Ethiopia as the country faces fears of renewed conflict in Tigray and tensions with Eritrea.
cards.body:
Ethiopia held a national election amid significant security challenges, with voting suspended in some areas due to safety concerns. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's party is widely expected to dominate the results.

The election takes place as the country faces serious instability, including fears of renewed conflict in the Tigray region and mounting tensions with neighboring Eritrea over Red Sea access. Security issues in parts of the country disrupted the normal electoral process, raising concerns about the overall legitimacy and completeness of the vote.

cards.headline: Britain Bars Entry to Social Media Personalities Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker
cards.teaser: UK authorities denied entry to two popular social media commentators, citing public good concerns.
cards.body:
UK Home Office authorities denied entry to American political commentators Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker, citing that their presence may not be conducive to the public good. Both men operate popular left-wing content channels with substantial online followings.

The pair were scheduled to speak at SXSW London festival and at Oxford this week. The Home Office provided no explanation for the decision to bar them from entering the country.

cards.headline: UK Releases Additional Files on Former Diplomat Peter Mandelson
cards.teaser: More than a thousand pages of documents revealed new details about the ex-diplomat fired over links to Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
The British government released more than a thousand pages of documents related to Peter Mandelson, the former diplomat who was dismissed from his position due to his connections with Jeffrey Epstein. The files included a letter in which Mandelson made claims about his tenure.

Mandelson previously served as UK ambassador to the United States before his firing. The document release follows earlier disclosures about his relationship with the convicted sex offender Epstein. The new files contain messages in which Mandelson criticized leadership and called for a complete revamp of government operations.

cards.headline: Alberta to Hold Vote on Separation From Canada
cards.teaser: Albertans will decide in October whether they want to remain part of Canada or hold a referendum on independence.
cards.body:
Alberta will hold a vote in October allowing residents to express whether they want to stay in Canada or proceed with a referendum on separation. The vote represents a significant moment for the separatist movement that has gained traction in the western Canadian province.

The outcome could either settle the question of Alberta's place in the Canadian federation or deepen the existing rift between the province and the federal government. Alberta has long harbored grievances about its treatment within Canada, particularly regarding resource revenue and federal policies.

cards.headline: Syrian Officials Face War Crimes Trial in Austria
cards.teaser: Two Assad regime officers who lived in Austria go on trial in the country's first prosecution of Syrian government officials.
cards.body:
Austria has opened its first trial against two officers from the Assad regime, accused of torture. The defendants allegedly lived undetected in Austria before their arrest and prosecution.

The trial provides a significant opportunity for Syrian witnesses to directly confront the men they have accused of committing war crimes. This proceeding marks Austria's participation in international efforts to hold Syrian government officials accountable for alleged abuses.

cards.headline: British soldier killed in training accident in northern Iraq
cards.teaser: A British soldier has died in a training exercise accident in northern Iraq.
cards.body:
Defence Secretary John Healey announced the death of a British soldier in the House of Commons on Monday. The soldier was killed during a training exercise in northern Iraq.

British forces maintain a presence in Iraq as part of ongoing military cooperation and training missions in the region.

cards.headline: Colorado elections clerk Tina Peters released from prison after sentence commutation
cards.teaser: Tina Peters, a former county clerk and election denier, was released from prison after her sentence was commuted.
cards.body:
Tina Peters, the former Mesa County clerk who became known for election denial claims, was released from prison following a commutation of her sentence. Her release has divided the Colorado community where she served.

Peters had been serving time related to her role in election-related activities in Mesa County. Governor Polis commuted her sentence, leading to her release. The decision has generated controversy and differing reactions across the state.

cards.headline: UK bars entry to US political commentators Cenk Uygur and Hasan Piker
cards.teaser: The UK Home Office denied entry to two left-wing US commentators who were scheduled to speak at events in London and Oxford.
cards.body:
The UK Home Office denied entry to American political commentators Hasan Piker and Cenk Uygur this week. Both are left-wing content creators with substantial online audiences and were scheduled to speak at SXSW London and events at Oxford.

Piker attributed the ban to remarks he made regarding Israel. The entry denial has drawn criticism from free speech advocates who oppose the UK authorities' decision to bar the US citizens from the country.

cards.headline: London Underground strikes set for Tuesday and Thursday
cards.teaser: Members of the RMT union will strike twice this week after talks to resolve a dispute over working hours failed.
cards.body:
London Underground workers will go on strike on Tuesday and Thursday following the collapse of negotiations. Members of the RMT union are striking over a dispute concerning working hours.

The strikes will affect Tube services across London. Talks between the union and transport authorities failed to produce an agreement that would have prevented the work stoppages scheduled for this week.

cards.headline: Serena Williams to return to tennis in doubles at Queen's
cards.teaser: Serena Williams will play competitive tennis for the first time in nearly four years.
cards.body:
Serena Williams will make her return to competitive tennis after nearly four years away, competing in women's doubles at Queen's. The 44-year-old tennis legend's comeback marks a significant moment for the sport.

Williams is widely regarded as one of the greatest players in tennis history. Her decision to resume competition in doubles rather than singles represents an important step in her return to the game.

cards.headline: Southampton orchestrated spying campaign against Championship rivals
cards.teaser: New WhatsApp messages reveal how Southampton conducted surveillance operations against competing teams.
cards.body:
WhatsApp messages have revealed that Southampton orchestrated a spying campaign against their Championship rivals. The messages show communication between individuals discussing the surveillance efforts, with one message reading "You legend. Manager loved it."

The revelations expose how the club conducted intelligence operations against competing teams in the Championship. The messages provide evidence of organized efforts to gather information about rival clubs during the season.

cards.headline: Barry Diller's People Inc. Offers to Buy MGM Resorts for $18 Billion
cards.teaser: The media mogul's company is preparing a takeover bid for the casino giant at $48.30 per share.
cards.body:
People Inc., the digital media company chaired by Barry Diller, has proposed acquiring all of MGM Resorts at a valuation exceeding $18 billion, or $48.30 per share. The bid would give People Inc. full ownership of the casino operator.

The move represents a significant strategic shift for Diller. Just weeks earlier, in late April, he told shareholders that People would focus more intently on its existing MGM stake, describing the stock as "wildly undervalued." The takeover proposal now seeks to capitalize on that assessment by taking complete control of the casino company.

cards.headline: Chinese Military Sought Restricted Nvidia Chips for Years, Records Show
cards.teaser: An analysis of procurement records suggests the People's Liberation Army has openly tried to acquire restricted U.S. technology.
cards.body:
The Chinese military sought to obtain Nvidia chips for years despite U.S. restrictions on the technology, according to an analysis of procurement records. The review covered six years of documents from the People's Liberation Army.

The records suggest that Chinese military entities openly attempted to acquire restricted American technology through procurement processes. Nvidia produces advanced chips used for artificial intelligence and other computing applications. The U.S. government has imposed restrictions on the export of certain high-performance chips to China over national security concerns.

cards.headline: Remote Work Linked to Rising Youth Unemployment, Federal Reserve Study Finds
cards.teaser: A New York Fed study points to remote work, rather than artificial intelligence, as a factor hurting young job seekers.
cards.body:
A New York Federal Reserve study has found that remote work arrangements are contributing to higher unemployment among young workers. The shift away from in-person employment has made it harder for recent graduates and entry-level job seekers to secure positions, as they miss out on traditional in-person training and networking opportunities.

The research challenges the widespread assumption that artificial intelligence is the primary cause of weak hiring among junior employees. Instead, the structural changes in how companies operate are disadvantaging younger workers in the job market.

cards.headline: UAW Strikes at General Motors Supplier Plant in Michigan
cards.teaser: Workers walked off the job at an axle plant that supplies GM, potentially threatening pickup truck production.
cards.body:
United Auto Workers members went on strike at an American Axle plant in Three Rivers, Michigan, which supplies components to General Motors. The work stoppage could threaten production at GM pickup truck plants within weeks if the dispute is not resolved.

Striking workers picketed outside the facility. Union members said wages have barely increased in 18 years. The axle plant produces parts essential to GM's truck manufacturing operations, and an extended strike could force shutdowns at assembly plants that depend on the supplier.

cards.headline: All-Electric Aircraft Completes Test Flight in New York City
cards.teaser: A new electric aircraft made a test flight, offering a glimpse at potential changes in air travel technology.
cards.body:
An all-electric aircraft conducted a test flight in New York City, demonstrating emerging technology in aviation. The flight represents a step toward electric-powered air travel as manufacturers explore alternatives to traditional jet fuel.

The aircraft test comes as the aviation industry faces pressure to reduce emissions and develop more sustainable transportation options. Electric planes could change how short-distance flights operate, though significant technical and regulatory hurdles remain before widespread commercial use becomes feasible.

cards.headline: UK Banks Offered Access to OpenAI Cyber Tool After Rival Blocks Preview
cards.teaser: Nine banks received an offer to use GPT 5.5 Cyber after Anthropic restricted access to its competing product.
cards.body:
Nine UK banks have been offered access to OpenAI's GPT 5.5 Cyber tool following Anthropic's decision to block previews of its competing Mythos cybersecurity AI tool.

The development underscores intensifying competition among AI providers seeking to serve the financial sector's cybersecurity needs. Banks are actively evaluating different AI solutions to enhance their defenses against cyber threats.

hero.headline: Nvidia releases first superchip for AI-powered Windows laptops
hero.body:
Nvidia has launched a new "superchip" designed to bring artificial intelligence capabilities directly to Windows laptops and desktop computers, marking the company's entry into the consumer PC processor market. The move intensifies competition with Intel, Apple, Qualcomm, and AMD.

The RTX Spark chip combines a microprocessor with a graphics processor and was developed in collaboration with Taiwan's MediaTek. It is designed to run AI agents locally on computers rather than relying on cloud computing servers. According to Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, the technology will allow AI agents to navigate PCs autonomously, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard interactions.

Major computer manufacturers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus, and HP will integrate the RTX Spark chip into their devices, paired with Microsoft's Windows software. Microsoft has already unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra as the first device featuring the technology. Huang announced the development at the Computex conference in Taiwan, following three years of collaboration between Nvidia and Microsoft.

Huang described the chip as "reimagining the PC for the first time in 40 years." Despite the chip's power, Nvidia stated that computers using it will remain thin and light. The unified memory design allows the processor and graphics chip to share data more efficiently than traditional laptop architectures.

The RTX Spark represents Nvidia's expansion beyond its dominant position in data center AI processors. The company is also developing the Vera central processing unit for AI agents, with early adopters including OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX.

Industry analysts view the move as strategically significant but a longer-term growth opportunity. Neil Shah of Counterpoint Research compared the RTX Spark's potential impact to major technological shifts like the iPhone and ChatGPT, suggesting it could transform PCs into "agentic AI personal computers."

Nvidia's push into consumer PCs comes as the industry attempts to revive PC sales by promoting AI features as a reason for customers to upgrade older machines. However, analysts note this business line will take time to generate substantial revenue, with Nvidia's current earnings still overwhelmingly dependent on demand for AI infrastructure and data center computing.

The launch has prompted competitive responses. Intel announced it will ship an AI chip later this year using cheaper memory and cooling technology than Nvidia and AMD competitors. Intel's new graphics processing unit, codenamed Crescent Island, is "purpose-built for this upcoming AI generation of agents," according to Anil Nanduri, vice-president of AI products at Intel's Data Center Group.

The RTX Spark is scheduled for release this year, signaling the start of a new competitive battleground in the semiconductor industry as major tech companies race to dominate the emerging market for AI-capable personal computers.

cards.headline: Dell launches $599 XPS 13 laptop to compete with MacBook Neo
cards.teaser: Dell introduced a new version of its XPS 13 laptop priced at $599, positioning the device as an alternative to Apple's MacBook Neo.
cards.body:
Dell unveiled the XPS 13 laptop at a starting price of $599, with a regular price of $699. The company is offering a temporary discount on the device. The laptop uses Intel's Wildcat Lake processor and represents Dell's attempt to offer a lower-cost alternative in the premium laptop category.

The device competes directly with Apple's MacBook Neo in design and pricing. Dell reintroduced the XPS 13 brand specifically to challenge Apple's position in the thin-and-light laptop market. Reuters, Engadget, and The Verge reported on the launch.

cards.headline: Intel announces air-cooled AI chip designed to undercut Nvidia and AMD
cards.teaser: Intel said its upcoming Crescent Island AI chip will operate without liquid cooling and cost less than competing products from Nvidia and AMD.
cards.body:
Intel is developing Crescent Island, an air-cooled processor built for artificial intelligence workloads that will cost less than competing chips from Nvidia and AMD. The chip uses LPDDR5 memory and requires no liquid cooling system.

The air-cooled design simplifies data center infrastructure while reducing power consumption and operating costs. Intel positions Crescent Island as a cost-effective option for organizations deploying AI systems, offering a practical alternative to more expensive, power-intensive competitors.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, creates booms heard across US and Canada
cards.teaser: A meteor entered the atmosphere over Massachusetts and exploded, producing loud booms reported across the United States and Canada.
cards.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT. The American Meteor Society identified the object as roughly 3 feet wide. At the time of breakup, it was traveling at 75,000 miles per hour at an altitude of 40 miles.

The explosion generated sonic booms heard across a wide region, with reports coming from as far south as Delaware and north into Montreal. NASA indicated that fragments from the meteor may have landed in Cape Cod Bay.

cards.headline: DuckDuckGo launches browser extensions for no-AI search
cards.teaser: DuckDuckGo released browser extensions for Chrome and Firefox that provide access to its search engine without artificial intelligence features.
cards.body:
The alternative search engine DuckDuckGo has launched browser extensions for Chrome and Firefox that let users search without AI-generated results or summaries. The extensions make it easier for users to access DuckDuckGo's traditional search results as a privacy-focused alternative to mainstream search services.

The move reflects a broader shift in the search market, where major search engines have integrated AI features into their core products. DuckDuckGo's traffic has increased significantly, positioning the extensions as a way to capitalize on user demand for AI-free search options.

cards.headline: Apple delays smart glasses release until late 2027
cards.teaser: Apple pushed back the launch of its smart glasses product to late 2027, according to reports from CNET and Bloomberg.
cards.body:
Apple changed the timeline for releasing its smart glasses, with the product now expected in late 2027. Bloomberg reported that Apple is using a strategy similar to its approach with the Apple Watch, starting with a premium product before expanding to broader price points. The company also plans a lighter, cheaper version of its Vision Pro headset for late 2028.

The Verge noted that Apple's glasses strategy mirrors its smartwatch rollout. 9to5Mac said the delay has increased interest in the product category. MacRumors reported on the timing for the Vision Pro successor.

cards.headline: Revolut begins rolling out services to users in India
cards.teaser: British fintech company Revolut started providing services to thousands of users in India ahead of a broader launch in the country.
cards.body:
Revolut has started rolling out its financial services to users in India, drawing on a waitlist of roughly 450,000 people. The British fintech is moving forward with a phased approach as it prepares for a wider expansion in the Indian market.

The company is using this initial rollout to test its services with a limited user base before making access available to more of its waitlisted users and the general public.

hero.headline: Serena Williams to return to professional tennis at Queen's Club
hero.body:
Serena Williams will make her competitive tennis comeback at 44 years old, playing in the women's doubles event at Queen's Club in London next week. This marks her first professional match in nearly four years, since she last competed at the 2022 US Open.

Williams has been cleared to return after rejoining the professional tennis drug testing pool six months ago. She will compete for a wildcard spot in the doubles draw alongside Victoria Mboko, a 19-year-old Canadian ranked number 9 in singles. The Queen's Club tournament is a WTA 500 event beginning on June 8, just one day after the French Open concludes.

The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion has been preparing for this return while training in Florida. She has been working with Alycia Parks, currently ranked number 79, and posted a video of them practicing together in March. While Williams did not formally announce her retirement in 2022, she appeared on the retired players' list until her recent return to the drug testing pool.

The announcement has generated excitement throughout the tennis world. Fellow competitors have expressed enthusiasm about her return. Naomi Osaka, who recently encountered Williams at the Met Gala this month, said: "I think it's good for me. I'll be very entertained. But overall the scope of it, I think it will bring people to watch tennis, which she always does bring an audience with her. I'm going to be tuned into the first match, for sure. Everyone knows Serena and [her sister] Venus were my role models growing up, so it's going to be cool to see her on the grounds again."

Madison Keys, ranked number 19, added: "Serena Williams playing tennis is only good for tennis. Let's be real, we all want to watch Serena. I am excited. She's the GOAT so it would be amazing if she came back. You get to watch history every single time she takes the court, so why not watch more?"

The WTA has celebrated Williams' return to the professional stage, recognizing her significant impact on the sport over more than two decades at elite level. Queen's Club represents a strategic choice for her comeback, as the grass court tournament traditionally precedes Wimbledon and allows players to prepare for the summer grass court season.

Williams has not disclosed her long-term competitive plans beyond the Queen's Club event. Her decision to return through doubles rather than singles suggests a cautious approach to assessing her physical condition and competitive readiness. The Queen's appearance will provide the first indication of whether this represents a brief return to the sport or the beginning of a more sustained comeback.

cards.headline: Six people stabbed during Arsenal victory parade in London
cards.teaser: Violence marred Arsenal's Premier League trophy celebration as six people were stabbed and 75 others required rescue from heights.
cards.body:
Six people were stabbed in north London following Arsenal's victory parade on Sunday evening, according to police. The Metropolitan Police said the stabbings occurred after most crowds had dispersed, with 24 people arrested in connection with the incidents.

Hundreds of thousands of fans lined the streets around Emirates Stadium to celebrate Arsenal's men's team winning the Premier League for the first time since 2004 and the women's team claiming the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup. During the parade, emergency services rescued approximately 75 people from height and made 16 arrests.

cards.headline: Paralympic shot putter died in accident with metal bar
cards.teaser: A Paralympic athlete was killed when a metal bar fell on him in what a court described as an accident waiting to happen.
cards.body:
A Paralympic athlete died when a metal bar fell on him during what prosecutors described as an accident waiting to happen. The fatal incident was examined during a sentencing hearing at the Old Bailey in London.

The characterization by prosecutors suggests that safety failures or negligence contributed to the death of the shot putter.

cards.headline: French Open fines player $76,000 for sexist comment about umpire
cards.teaser: Paraguayan tennis player Adolfo Daniel Vallejo received one of the largest fines in tennis history for making a sexist remark about a female chair umpire.
cards.body:
Adolfo Daniel Vallejo of Paraguay was fined $76,000 by the French Open for making sexist comments about a female chair umpire. Tournament organizers described the remarks as "clearly unacceptable" following his exit from the competition.

The substantial penalty reflects Roland Garros' commitment to addressing discriminatory behavior at the clay court Grand Slam in Paris.

cards.headline: Chicago Bears stadium bill stalls in Illinois legislature
cards.teaser: The Bears' pursuit of a new stadium in Illinois hit a major obstacle as state lawmakers adjourned without passing stadium funding legislation.
cards.body:
Illinois lawmakers adjourned without passing a bill that would have provided funding for a new Chicago Bears stadium, keeping alive the possibility the team could relocate to Indiana. The failure came as a last-minute setback in the Bears' efforts to secure state support for a new facility.

The Bears released a statement following the $55 billion Illinois budget passage that did not include stadium provisions. A megaprojects bill was revamped as an amendment to House Bill 958, but failed to gain enough support before the legislative session ended.

cards.headline: Boxing promoter calls for Tom Aspinall's release from UFC contract
cards.teaser: Eddie Hearn urged UFC president Dana White to release heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall, claiming the fighter is underpaid.
cards.body:
Boxing promoter Eddie Hearn called on UFC president Dana White to release Tom Aspinall from his contract, arguing the heavyweight champion is not receiving fair compensation for his worth. Hearn made a public plea on behalf of the British fighter.

Hearn also made promises regarding fellow British boxer Conor Benn during his appeal to White. The promoter's comments highlight ongoing tensions between boxing and mixed martial arts organizations over fighter pay and contract terms.

cards.headline: Mary Earps and Mapi Leon set to join London City Lionesses
cards.teaser: Former England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Spain defender Mapi Leon are close to signing with London City Lionesses.
cards.body:
Former England goalkeeper Mary Earps and Spain defender Mapi Leon are poised to join London City Lionesses this summer. The dual signing would strengthen the club's squad with experienced international players.

Both athletes bring significant credentials from their respective national teams to the women's soccer club.

hero.headline: Dua Lipa Marries Callum Turner in London Ceremony
hero.body:
Dua Lipa married actor Callum Turner in a low-key London ceremony, wearing a wedding outfit that paid homage to Bianca Jagger's iconic 1971 bridal look. The singer chose a custom suit instead of a traditional wedding dress for her first wedding look, channeling the style of the original cool girl bride.

The intimate ceremony took place in London with a private guest list. Lipa's fashion choice referenced Jagger's famous white skirt suit worn when she married Mick Jagger in Saint-Tropez over five decades ago. The look represented a departure from conventional bridal gowns and aligned with a growing trend of brides choosing alternative wedding attire.

Lipa, known for hits including "Levitating" and "Don't Start Now," has been in a relationship with Turner, who recently appeared in the film "Masters of the Air." The couple kept details of their relationship largely private before the wedding. Turner's acting credits include roles in the "Fantastic Beasts" franchise and the Apple TV+ series.

The wedding suit was custom-made for the occasion, continuing Lipa's pattern of making bold fashion statements at major life events. Jagger's 1971 wedding look has remained influential in bridal fashion, with many brides over the years opting for suits or non-traditional attire inspired by her choice. The original look featured a wide-brimmed hat and a jacket with a skirt, creating a sophisticated alternative to the typical wedding dress.

The ceremony's low-key nature contrasted with Lipa's high-profile career and public presence. Neither Lipa nor Turner had publicly announced engagement plans before the wedding. The couple's decision to keep the event intimate reflects a trend among celebrities opting for smaller, more private ceremonies rather than elaborate public weddings.

cards.headline: 20-Year-Old YouTuber Kane Parsons Directs Summer Box Office Hit With Backrooms
cards.teaser: Kane Parsons, creator of online phenomenon Backrooms, was still in high school when filmmaker James Wan first reached out to collaborate on the film.
cards.body:
Kane Parsons has become the youngest filmmaker to open a film at number one at the North American box office with his directorial debut, Backrooms. At 20 years old, he surpassed the previous record held by Josh Trank, who was 27 when his film Chronicle opened in 2011.

The film's success exceeded industry expectations, earning $81 million in its first weekend—a record for studio A24. Parsons transformed his YouTube series concept into the theatrical release, with James Wan's production company helping develop the online phenomenon for the big screen.

cards.headline: New York Times Publisher Criticizes AI Companies Over Content Use
cards.teaser: A.G. Sulzberger warned that AI developers are making choices that could harm the news industry and public access to reliable information.
cards.body:
New York Times publisher A.G. Sulzberger warned that generative AI companies are making unlawful choices that threaten news organizations and undermine public access to reliable information. Speaking at the World News Media Congress in France, he criticized how AI developers use journalistic content to train their systems without proper authorization.

Sulzberger's remarks highlight growing tension between the media industry and technology companies over intellectual property rights and fair compensation for content used in AI development.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Releases Horror-Themed Music Video With Justin Long
cards.teaser: Grande's video for Hate That I Made You Love Me features actor Justin Long and cinematography by Steven Spielberg's regular collaborator Janusz Kaminski.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande released a horror-inspired music video for her single Hate That I Made You Love Me, co-starring actor Justin Long. Director Christian Breslauer helmed the project, having previously worked with Grande on the short film Brighter Days Ahead from her 2024 album Eternal Sunshine.

Janusz Kaminski, Steven Spielberg's frequent cinematographer, shot the video. The visual represents Grande's latest single release and marks another collaboration between the singer and Breslauer.

cards.headline: Actors on Actors Returns With Jennifer Aniston, Kit Harington and Jamie Lee Curtis
cards.teaser: The 24th season of the interview series will feature Emmy contenders including reunions of Friends and Game of Thrones cast members.
cards.body:
Variety and CNN announced the lineup for the 24th season of Actors on Actors, featuring major contenders for this year's Emmy Awards. The interview series will include Jennifer Aniston and Lisa Kudrow from Friends, Kit Harington and Peter Dinklage from Game of Thrones, and Tracy Morgan with Marcello Hernández from their respective projects.

The award-winning series pairs actors for in-depth conversations about their craft and recent work. The season focuses on performers considered front-runners in various Emmy categories, bringing together both longtime collaborators and new pairings.

cards.headline: ESPN Expands Rights Deal With Women's National Football Conference
cards.teaser: The two-year agreement will keep the WNFC championship game on ESPN2 and add additional coverage of women's tackle football.
cards.body:
ESPN and the Women's National Football Conference have extended their broadcast rights agreement for two years. The WNFC IX Cup Championship Game will continue to air on ESPN2 under the new deal.

The expanded partnership brings more women's tackle football to ESPN viewers, reflecting increased audience interest in the sport. The agreement includes coverage beyond the championship game, giving fans greater access to league programming.

cards.headline: Disney Princess Concert Tour Announces U.K. and Ireland Dates
cards.teaser: The musical experience themed around Disney Princesses will launch in Warwick in March 2027 before touring major cities.
cards.body:
Disney Princess: The Concert will debut in Warwick in March 2027, followed by a tour across the U.K. and Ireland. The production will make stops in Swansea, Brighton, Hull, Manchester and other cities throughout the region.

The musical experience centers on songs and themes from Disney Princess films. The tour represents Disney's theatrical offerings expanding into the U.K.

hero.headline: Jill Biden says Trump pardon was needed to protect Hunter from targeting
hero.teaser: Former first lady defends her stepson's pardon in new interview, citing concerns about incoming administration.
hero.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden has defended the presidential pardon issued to her stepson, Hunter Biden, explaining that the decision became necessary after Donald Trump's election victory.

In a recent interview, Jill Biden stated that the circumstances surrounding the pardon changed once Trump won the presidency. "When [President] Trump was elected, things changed, and we knew that he would target Hunter, and we just could not let our son go to jail on a charge that no one would," she said.

The pardon, issued by former President Joe Biden before leaving office, covered federal charges that had been brought against Hunter Biden. According to Jill Biden's account, the family's decision to support the pardon was motivated by concerns about how Trump might use his position to pursue her stepson.

Jill Biden's comments suggest that the pardon was partly a protective measure against potential future prosecution. She emphasized that Hunter faced charges that were not typically prosecuted against others, implying the case against him was unusual or politically motivated.

The former first lady's remarks come as she prepares to release a new memoir titled "View from the East Wing," which documents her experiences during her time in the White House. The book is expected to include her perspective on her husband's 2024 presidential campaign and his decision to withdraw from the race.

Jill Biden has remained a steadfast supporter of her husband throughout his long political career. However, her recent comments about the pardon have drawn scrutiny from some observers. A former spokesperson for Jill Biden suggested that her current statements about events in the White House may have damaged her credibility, noting that she is now saying things "completely different" from what she said previously.

The pardon decision sparked considerable public debate when it was announced. While some viewed it as a father protecting his son from legal jeopardy, others criticized it as an abuse of presidential power. The former first lady's explanation that Trump would have targeted Hunter appears to be her fullest public justification for supporting the controversial pardon.

Jill Biden's upcoming memoir is likely to provide additional context about the pardon decision and other significant moments from the Biden presidency. Her willingness to discuss the pardon in interviews suggests she intends to address the controversy directly in the book, offering her perspective on one of the most debated decisions of the Biden administration's final days.

cards.headline: Hezbollah signals readiness for immediate ceasefire with Israel
cards.teaser: Lebanese parliament speaker tells Trump administration that Hezbollah will accept full ceasefire and guarantee its implementation.
cards.body:
Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri conveyed to the Trump administration that Hezbollah is prepared for a full and immediate ceasefire with Israel. Berri's adviser Ali Hamdan confirmed the communication took place on Sunday and stated that Hezbollah would guarantee implementation of any agreement.

The signal comes as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered strikes on Beirut's Dahieh suburb, a Hezbollah stronghold, in response to attacks on Israeli civilians. Iran's negotiators continue discussions aimed at resolving the broader regional conflict.

cards.headline: Trump administration closes AI chip export loophole for Chinese-owned firms
cards.teaser: Commerce Department clarifies that licenses are required to sell advanced chips to companies with Chinese parents, regardless of location.
cards.body:
The Trump administration issued new Commerce Department guidance on Sunday to tighten restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chip exports. The clarification requires licenses for sales of these chips to firms with Chinese parent companies, even if the purchasing entity operates outside China or other restricted countries.

The move addresses a gap officials identified in 2023 export control requirements. By extending restrictions based on corporate ownership rather than just the physical location of the buyer, the administration aims to prevent companies from circumventing existing limitations on advanced chip sales.

cards.headline: US military kills three in fourth drug interdiction strike this week
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. military conducted another strike on a boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean over the weekend, killing three people aboard. This marks the fourth such attack in a week, bringing the total death toll from these operations to 205. U.S. Southern Command said the vessel was carrying drugs.

The strikes represent an intensification of military involvement in counter-narcotics operations in the region, shifting from traditional Coast Guard-led boarding and seizure tactics to lethal force operations.

cards.headline: Becerra leads California governor race ahead of primary vote
cards.teaser: Former Health and Human Services Secretary holds six-point advantage in final polling before primary election.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra holds a six-point lead in the California gubernatorial primary race as voters prepare to cast ballots on June 2. An Emerson College Polling/Inside California Politics survey released Saturday showed Becerra receiving support from 28 percent of voters.

Billionaire candidates are among those trailing Becerra in the polling. The primary will determine which candidates advance to the general election for governor of the nation's most populous state.

cards.headline: Former Biden spokesperson says Jill Biden damaged credibility with memoir remarks
cards.teaser: Ex-spokesperson questions consistency of former first lady's statements about President Biden during book tour.
cards.body:
A former spokesperson for Jill Biden said her credibility was damaged by remarks she made about former President Biden during a promotional tour for her new memoir. The spokesperson pointed out inconsistencies between what the former first lady is saying now and her previous statements.

In recent interviews promoting the book, Jill Biden defended the pardon her husband issued to her stepson Hunter Biden. She suggested that the pardon was necessary because President Trump's election meant Hunter would face targeting.

cards.headline: Study finds brief AI use reduces focus and problem-solving ability
cards.teaser: New research shows artificial intelligence can compromise cognitive function in a relatively short period.
cards.body:
Scientists have found that using artificial intelligence for just minutes can reduce focus and persistence, according to a new study. The research indicates AI can compromise cognitive function and problem-solving abilities in a relatively short time frame.

The study adds to growing research on how AI tools affect human cognition and work habits. The findings suggest even brief interactions with AI systems may have measurable impacts on how people approach tasks and sustain concentration.
